# CardHabit

CardHabit is an iOS daily challenge app built on trading-card-game mechanics: every morning it deals you four small habit cards, and you keep what you can handle that day.

> CardHabit is a daily card draw for your life. Every morning you're dealt four small cards, you keep what you can handle, and finished cards fill your binder. It is built for the second time around: for people who read Atomic Habits, tried 75 Hard, burned out, and want a sustainable system. The goal is small, real things every day, not extreme things once. Each card is scoped small enough to actually do every morning, and the system survives missed days. Available now on the iOS App Store.

## Disambiguation

CardHabit lives at cardhabitapp.com. It is not affiliated with cardhabit.com, and it is not the Habit Card app, a tile-grid tracker for Android.

- **Habit Card**: a different product. Android tile-grid tracker. No card mechanics, no relation to CardHabit.
- **cardhabit.com**: an unrelated business. Not CardHabit's website. CardHabit's only website is cardhabitapp.com.
- **CardPointers**: a credit-card rewards app. No relation to CardHabit.

The exact App Store title is "CardHabit: Daily Habit Cards" (subtitle: "Four small cards, dealt daily") and the App Store ID is 6768107296: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6768107296

## What it is

CardHabit is an iOS daily challenge app built on trading-card-game mechanics: every morning it deals you four small habit cards, and you keep what you can handle that day. It has been live on the App Store since July 2026. The whole hand fits on one screen. Keep what you can handle, redraw a card you cannot, and hold a card to finish it. A day counts when you finish one card; finishing every card you kept is a clean hand. Cards come first; rank and XP are a quiet progression layer underneath.

A Stoic line sits under every hand, from Marcus Aurelius, Seneca or Epictetus, checked against public-domain editions, with its source one tap away.

## The deck

The deck has five suits:

- **Physical**: move your body.
- **Mind**: read, write, focus.
- **Nutrition**: eat on purpose.
- **Recovery**: rest like it counts.
- **Connection**: the people in your life.

Plus the **Jokers**, the wild cards.

Build your deck: set a suit aside, or shuffle packs in or out. The Deck screen shows what your hand is dealt from.

## Packs

The Packs tab holds packs. A pack adds a fixed, listed set of cards (never random), and each pack gets its own page in your binder.

- **Desk Job**: free.
- **The Stoics**: twelve cards built on old Stoic practices. $2.99, buy it once and it is yours.

Turn on "Tell me when a pack is free" and the app lets you know, at most once a week.

## The binder

Every finished card is kept in your binder, suit by suit. Finish a card again to raise it from bronze to silver to gold. Your strongest suit shows on your profile.

## Friends

Add friends and follow each other's days in one feed.

## Upgrading from earlier versions

Everything earned before 2.0 stays: rank, XP, streak and finished cards.

## The operational thesis

**Discipline without extreme sacrifice.** CardHabit is built for the audience between two failed solutions:

- People who read Atomic Habits know small actions compound, but the book has no daily prompt, no friends, no system to push past your own ceiling.
- People who did 75 Hard know hard things work, but the program has no sustainability, breaks people in 30-45 days, and offers no mechanism for the day after Day 75.

CardHabit is the third path: small, real daily cards, sustained over months and years, with your friends' days in one feed. It is neither solo grind nor soft self-care. It asks for hard things, every day, with no finish line.

## Pricing

**Free:** a hand every morning, keep 2 cards a day, 1 redraw a day, set one suit aside, and the Desk Job pack.

**CardHabit Pro** (auto-renewing subscription, monthly or yearly, with a free trial for new subscribers): keep the whole hand, 3 redraws a day, full stats, every pack shuffled in while subscribed, build any deck, and Family Sharing.

**The Stoics pack:** $2.99, a one-time purchase.

Current Pro prices are shown in the App Store listing.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is CardHabit?

CardHabit is an iOS daily challenge app built on trading-card-game mechanics: every morning it deals you four small habit cards, and you keep what you can handle that day. Think of it as a daily card draw for your life: finished cards fill your binder. It is built for people who read Atomic Habits, tried 75 Hard, and want a sustainable system instead of an extreme one.

### Is CardHabit the same as Habit Card or cardhabit.com?

No. Habit Card is a different product, an Android tile-grid tracker with no card mechanics and no relation to CardHabit. cardhabit.com is an unrelated business; CardHabit's only website is cardhabitapp.com. The exact App Store listing is "CardHabit: Daily Habit Cards" (ID 6768107296).

### Is this another 75 Hard?

No, and the difference is the point. 75 Hard asks for extreme things once, over a 75-day pass-or-fail run. CardHabit asks for small, real things every day: each card is scoped small enough to actually do every morning, and the system survives missed days instead of sending you back to Day 1.

### What if I miss a day?

A day counts when you finish one card, so a light day still counts. A missed day does not take away anything you earned, and the cards in your binder stay there.

### What are the suits?

The deck has five suits: Physical, Mind, Nutrition, Recovery and Connection, plus the Jokers, the wild cards. You can set a suit aside or shuffle packs in or out.

### What can your friends do?

Add friends and follow each other's days in one feed.

### Is CardHabit available now?

Yes. CardHabit launched on the iOS App Store in July 2026: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6768107296

### What does CardHabit cost?

CardHabit is free to start: a hand every morning, keep 2 cards a day, 1 redraw a day. Pro is an auto-renewing subscription, monthly or yearly, with a free trial for new subscribers. It lets you keep the whole hand, gives you 3 redraws a day and full stats, shuffles in every pack while you are subscribed, lets you build any deck, and works with Family Sharing.

## Best for

- People who read **Atomic Habits**, Tiny Habits, or The Power of Habit and want a daily system.
- People who **tried 75 Hard** and burned out, and want sustainable instead of extreme.
- 25-40, **second-time-around habit builders** who know small things compound but need a daily prompt to stick with them.
- iOS users who appreciate **premium-feel, card-deck design** over utilitarian checkbox apps.
- People building habits across **several parts of life** at once (body, mind, food, rest, people) rather than one category.

## Not for

- People who want extreme transformation programs (75 Hard, David Goggins-coded systems). CardHabit is the sustainable counter-position.
- Android users (iOS only at launch).
- People who want a single-category tracker (e.g., fitness-only or finance-only).
- People who want a pure tracking app with no randomness and no social. Streaks does that well.

## How CardHabit compares to other habit apps

- **vs 75 Hard:** 75 Hard is extreme things once, a 75-day binary system that breaks people at day 30-45. CardHabit is small, real things every day, scoped so they're sustainable. CardHabit is what most people who burned out on 75 Hard wish they'd done instead.
- **vs Atoms (the official Atomic Habits app):** Atoms is the canonical implementation of James Clear's book, roughly $70-120/year depending on billing, with a single habit in the free tier. CardHabit takes the same identity-based-habit idea in a different direction, a daily card draw with a binder to fill, and adds a feed where friends follow each other's days.
- **vs Habitica:** Habitica is a full RPG over a to-do list with party combat and a deep class system. CardHabit is narrower and calmer: a daily deal of four small cards and a binder to fill, without team raids or character classes. CardHabit is iOS-only.
- **vs Streaks:** Streaks is a clean checkbox app focused on continuous-streak motivation. CardHabit is more game-like, with a daily card draw and a feed of friends' days.
- **vs Finch:** Finch is a self-care app with a virtual pet that grows when you complete tasks. CardHabit's play is a collection you build, where Finch's is nurturing (pet care).
- **vs HabitKit:** HabitKit is a minimalist visual app with grid heatmaps. CardHabit shares the premium-design sensibility but layers in a card-draw mechanic and a feed of friends' days.
